title: The single supplement, explained honestly
subtitle: You are not being penalised for travelling alone. You are being charged for the cabin.

text: A cruise fare is quoted per person but sold per cabin.
sub: The ship has a fixed number of cabins and no more. One occupant instead of two halves the revenue from a room the line cannot re-cut.

items.head: Dedicated solo cabins
items.body: Small ships increasingly build a handful. Very few per sailing, and they go first - book them a season out.

items.head: Reduced-supplement promotions
items.body: Lines run them on sailings that need help. River cruises in shoulder months are the reliable hunting ground.

items.head: River rather than ocean
items.body: Solo terms on European river itineraries are generally kinder than on comparable ocean sailings.

items.head: The quiet season
items.body: Late autumn on the Danube, the Aegean before the crowds. Fewer couples competing for the same cabin.

kicker: How to read a solo quote
title: Four things to check

points.label: The multiplier
points.value: Quoted as a percentage of the double fare. It varies widely by line and sailing.

points.label: What it covers
points.value: Some supplements exclude port fees and taxes, some include them.

points.label: Category limits
points.value: The kind terms often apply only to the lower cabin grades.

points.label: Included extras
points.value: Ask whether credit and inclusions are per cabin or per guest. It matters most solo.

quote: A solo traveller with flexible dates has more leverage than a couple with fixed ones. Use it.

text: Bring the sailing to the fare, not the fare to the sailing.
sub: Choose the region and the season you want, then let me find the weeks where solo terms are kindest. The itinerary rarely suffers for moving a fortnight.

title: Tell me the region and I'll find the weeks
body: Send me where you'd like to sail alone and roughly when. I'll come back with the sailings where the solo terms are worth having.
